headline: Chip Stocks Lead a Lopsided Tape as Consumer Names Slump
body_html:
Semiconductor stocks carried the market on Thursday, with the group up 3.47% at midday while the broader tape stayed mixed. Of the 664 stocks we track, 346 were higher and 315 lower, a slim edge that suggests the gains were concentrated in a few areas. Prices are not final.

The leadership was all AI infrastructure. Optical-networking firm Coherent jumped 10.4%, Ambarella rose 10.17%, Everpure gained 9.62% and Seagate added 7.37%. Software joined in, up 0.82%, with Rubrik up 8.99% and Zscaler up 7.69%. Energy gained 0.99% and financials 0.36%. On the other side, consumer shares fell 1.63% and homebuilders 1.49%, while materials slipped 0.49%. Williams-Sonoma dropped 7.45%, and Liquidity Services was the session's worst performer, down 20.22%.

Into the close, the question is whether the chip rally holds or fades, and whether the rotation away from consumer and housing names deepens. A strong finish for technology would argue the move has staying power. Traders will also be weighing that against Friday, November 20, the next session, and the geopolitical headlines out of the Middle East.

briefs.headline: Optical and storage names surge
briefs.body: Coherent climbed 10.4% to top our universe, while Everpure rose 9.62% and Seagate gained 7.37%. The moves show investors favoring the hardware that moves and stores data for AI workloads. Intraday gains can fade, so the closing print matters.

briefs.headline: Security software catches a bid
briefs.body: Rubrik advanced 8.99% and Zscaler gained 7.69%, helping the software group to a 0.82% rise. Cybersecurity names led a sector that was otherwise modestly higher, a sign buyers were selective rather than sweeping.

briefs.headline: Consumer shares retreat
briefs.body: The consumer group fell 1.63% and homebuilders lost 1.49%, the weakest pockets of the tape. Williams-Sonoma slid 7.45%, MINISO fell 7.14% and Universal Technical Institute dropped 6.25%, pointing to pressure across retail and education.

briefs.headline: Liquidity Services tumbles by a fifth
briefs.body: Liquidity Services fell 20.22%, the steepest decline among the stocks we track and far worse than any other laggard. The online-marketplace operator's drop stood out on a day when most of the market moved in single digits.

briefs.headline: Power demand from data centers in focus
briefs.body: The International Energy Agency said electricity use by data centers could double by 2030. That backdrop underpins interest in AI hardware, though Ionic Digital, a data-center and crypto-mining firm, fell 5.3% on the session.

briefs.headline: Iran remarks keep energy in view
briefs.body: President Trump said the US will 'see what happens' in its conflict with Iran after January 1. Energy shares rose 0.99% on the day, making the sector one of the stronger groups as traders weigh geopolitical risk.
